name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Little Flower
history: Discalced Carmelite friars dreamed of a national shrine to the newly canonized St. Thérèse of Lisieux, the Little Flower. The cornerstone was laid on 15 October 1929, just as the Great Depression began, and the church was finished in 1931. It is one of four minor basilicas in Texas.
arch: A Beaux-Arts church with a tall bell tower and domes, also called Our Lady of Mount Carmel and St. Thérèse.
features: It keeps three first-class relics of St. Thérèse, shown weekly for veneration.
A portrait of St. Thérèse sent by the Carmel of Lisieux was restored and reinstalled in 2007.

look.d: The tower rises over San Antonio's west side.
The domes cap a church built during the Great Depression.

fun: A friar went to France in 1927 to visit St. Thérèse's sisters, who sent back relics, books and her portrait.
journal: Built in the Depression for a young French saint. Texas roses for the Little Flower.
